'''Dorian Lawrence Finney-Smith''' (born May 4, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Charlotte Hornets]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech Hokies]] and [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida Gators]], and was named [[List of All-SEC men's basketball teams|All-SEC Second Team]] in 2015 and 2016 with the Gators.

After going undrafted in the 2016 NBA draft, Finney-Smith signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]], where he would spend seven seasons and become a full-time starter by 2019. He helped the team reach the [[NBA conference finals|Western Conference Finals]] in 2022.

Finney-Smith was traded to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in February 2023, and then to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in December 2024. He signed with the [[Houston Rockets]] during the 2025 off-season, where he would spend one year before being traded to the Hornets during the 2026 off-season.

==High school career==
Finney-Smith attended [[I. C. Norcom High School]] in [[Portsmouth, Virginia]]. As a junior in 2009–10, he averaged 19.7 points, 13 rebounds, six assists, three steals, and two blocks per game.<ref name=bio>{{cite web | url=http://www.floridagators.com/roster.aspx?rp_id=609 | title=Dorian Finney-Smith Bio | work=FloridaGators.com | accessdate=July 10, 2016}}</ref>

In September 2010, Finney-Smith committed to [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]],<ref>{{cite web | last=Fairbank | first=Dave | url=http://www.dailypress.com/sports/dp-spt-finney-smith-story.html | title=Top recruit Dorian Finney-Smith of Norcom says he'll play basketball for Virginia Tech | work=DailyPress.com | date=September 28, 2010 | accessdate=July 10, 2016}}</ref> and later signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] with the Hokies in December.<ref>{{cite web | last=Jones | first=Matt | url=http://www.collegiatetimes.com/news/virginia_tech/recruiting-class-provides-promising-future-for-tech-basketball/article_88a00bfb-6a8c-59f9-8970-945e5b70671e.html | title=2011 recruiting class provides promising future for Tech basketball | work=CollegiateTimes.com | date=December 7, 2010 | accessdate=July 10, 2016}}</ref>

As a senior at Norcom in 2010–11, Finney-Smith averaged 18 points, 10.7 rebounds, and 3.8 blocks per game. He led the team to back-to-back Group AAA state championships, along with Eastern Region and District titles. He recorded 19 points, 17 rebounds and three blocks in the state championship game as a senior. He finished his high school career as a two-time VHSL Class AAA Player of the Year and first-team all-state, all-region, All-Tidewater and all-district. He also earned All-Tidewater player of the year as a junior and co-player of the year as a senior.<ref name="bio" />

==College career==
As a freshman at [[Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball|Virginia Tech]] in 2011–12, Finney-Smith played in all 33 games, making 30 starts. He averaged 6.3 points and 7.0 rebounds per game and was named to the [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team. He scored a season-high 17 points in a 66–65 win over [[Boston College Eagles men's basketball|Boston College]].<ref name="bio" />

In June 2012, Finney-Smith transferred to [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]] and was forced to sit out the 2012–13 season due to NCAA transfer regulations.<ref>{{cite news | last=Borzello | first=Jeff | url=http://www.cbssports.com/collegebasketball/eye-on-college-basketball/19354869/source-dorian-finneysmith-transfers-to-florida | title=Source: Virginia Tech's Dorian Finney-Smith to transfer to Florida | work=CBSSports.com | date=June 14, 2012 | accessdate=July 10, 2016}}</ref>

As a sophomore in 2013–14, Finney-Smith was named [[Southeastern Conference|SEC]] Sixth Man of the Year, becoming just the second Gator to win the award after [[Chris Richard (basketball)|Chris Richard]] in 2007. He was Florida's leading rebounder, both in total rebounds (247) and per-game average (6.7). He also recorded the first 20/15 performance by a Gator in a road game during [[Billy Donovan]]'s tenure, totaling a personal-best 22 points in an overtime win over [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]]. He appeared in 37 games with two starting assignments, averaging 8.7 points, 6.7 rebounds, and 2.1 assists in 25.8 minutes per game.<ref name="bio" />

[[File:Dorian Finney-Smith Dunks Pre-Game.jpg|thumb|left|Finney-Smith dunking before a game in January 2015]]
As a junior in 2014–15, Finney-Smith was named second-team All-SEC by the coaches and was Florida's leading scorer (13.1), rebounder (6.2) and three-point shooter (.426). He scored a career-high 25 points in Florida's win over [[Jacksonville Dolphins men's basketball|Jacksonville]], including a 5-for-7 performance from three-point range.<ref name="bio" />

As a senior in 2015–16, Finney-Smith was named second-team All-SEC by the coaches and third-team All-SEC by the Associated Press. He was Florida's leading scorer (14.7) for the second straight season and top rebounder (8.3) for the third consecutive season. He became the first Florida player to join the 1,000-point club after transferring to the school mid-tenure. His 1,220 career points at Florida rank 36th in school history.<ref name="bio" />

==Professional career==
===Dallas Mavericks (2016–2023)===
====2016–2019: Early years====
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Finney-Smith signed with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] on July 8, and joined the team for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.mavs.com/mavericks-sign-forward-dorian-finney-smith/ | title=Mavericks sign forward Dorian Finney-Smith | work=Mavs.com | date=July 8, 2016 | accessdate=July 10, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Karalla | first=Bobby | url=http://www.mavs.com/dorian-finney-smith-brings-length-versatility-mavs/ | title=Dorian Finney-Smith brings more length, versatility to the Mavs | work=Mavs.com | date=July 9, 2010 | accessdate=July 10, 2016 | archive-date=October 24, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161024005637/http://www.mavs.com/dorian-finney-smith-brings-length-versatility-mavs/ | url-status=dead }}</ref> Finney-Smith secured an opening-night roster spot after impressing the Mavericks during training camp and preseason. After playing less than five minutes cumulatively over the first five games of the 2016–17 season, Finney-Smith played 31 minutes on November 6 against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]], including most of the second half and overtime.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899540|title=Barnes scores career-high 34, Mavs beat Bucks 86–75 in OT|publisher=ESPN|date=November 6, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}}</ref> He subsequently recorded five points, three rebounds, three steals and one block in an 86–75 win.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899540|title=Bucks vs. Mavericks – Box Score|publisher=ESPN|date=November 6, 2016|access-date=November 6, 2016}}</ref> Two days later, he made his first career start, scoring five points in a 109–97 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899554|title=Mavericks hold off Lakers 109–97 without Dirk, Deron|publisher=ESPN|date=November 8, 2016|access-date=November 9, 2016}}</ref> On December 9, he had a season-best game with career highs of 12 points and eight rebounds (equal game high) in a 111–103 win over the [[Indiana Pacers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899785|title=Matthews gets 26, Barnes 25 to lead Mavs past Pacers 111–103|publisher=ESPN|date=December 9, 2016|access-date=December 10, 2016}}</ref> On December 12, he had career highs in points and rebounds for the second straight home game, finishing with 13 points and nine boards in a 112–92 win over the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899807|title=Matthews leads Mavs to rare blowout, 112–92 over Nuggets|publisher=ESPN|date=December 12, 2016|access-date=December 13, 2016}}</ref>

On March 10, 2018, Finney-Smith played in his first game since November 12, 2017, after missing 51 straight games and 57 overall with left knee [[quadriceps]] [[tendinitis]]. He had seven points in 18 minutes in the Mavericks' 114–80 win over the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975735|title=Grizzlies drop 17th straight as Mavericks roll to 114–80 win|publisher=ESPN|date=March 10, 2018|access-date=March 10, 2018}}</ref> On April 6, he recorded season-highs of 15 points and ten rebounds in a 113–106 overtime loss to the [[Detroit Pistons]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks vs Detroit Pistons Apr 6, 2018 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021701181 |access-date=February 7, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

On November 2, 2018, Finney-Smith scored a season-high 19 points, alongside seven rebounds, two assists and two steals, in a 118–106 loss to the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=New York Knicks vs Dallas Mavericks Nov 2, 2018 Game Summary |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0021800121 |access-date=February 7, 2023 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

====2019–2023: Starting role and contract extension====
[[File:Cleveland Cavaliers vs. Dallas Mavericks (51176263161) (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Finney-Smith shoots the ball with the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in 2021]]
On July 11, 2019, Finney-Smith re-signed with the Mavericks<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mavs.com/mavericks-re-sign-forward-dorian-finney-smith/|title=Mavericks re-sign forward Dorian Finney-Smith|publisher=mavs.com|date=July 11, 2019|accessdate=July 11, 2019}}</ref> on a 3-year, $12 million contract.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mavericks re-sign restricted free agent Dorian Finney-Smith|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2019/07/11/mavericks-re-sign-restricted-free-agent-dorian-finney-smith/39677859/|access-date=August 10, 2020|work=USA Today}}</ref> On November 18, he had a then-career high 22 points in a 117–110 victory over the [[San Antonio Spurs]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Doncic, Finney-Smith Set Career Marks As Mavs Hold Off Spurs 117–110|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/doncic-finney-smith-set-career-marks-as-mavs-hold-off-spurs-117-110|access-date=August 9, 2020|magazine=Sports Illustrated |date=November 19, 2019 }}</ref> On August 4, 2020, Finney-Smith grabbed a career high 16 rebounds in a 114–110 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mavericks' Dorian Finney-Smith: Career-high 16 boards Tuesday|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mavericks-dorian-finney-smith-career-high-16-boards-tuesday/|access-date=August 9, 2020|website=CBSSports.com |date=August 4, 2020 }}</ref> On August 8, he had a then-career high 27 points and a career high six three pointers made in a 136–132 victory against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Mavericks' Dorian Finney-Smith: Career night in win over Milwaukee|url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/mavericks-dorian-finney-smith-career-night-in-win-over-milwaukee/|access-date=August 9, 2020|website=CBSSports.com |date=August 9, 2020 }}</ref> The Mavericks qualified for the postseason for the first time since [[2016 NBA playoffs|2016]] and faced the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] during their first round series. Finney-Smith made his playoff debut on August 17, recording nine points, four rebounds, two assists and two steals in a 118–110 Game 1 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=CLIPPERS HOLD OFF DONCIC, MAVS AFTER PORZINGIS IS TOSSED |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0041900151 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> The Mavericks were eventually eliminated in six games by the Clippers.

On April 5, 2021, Finney-Smith recorded a season-high 23 points, alongside six rebounds and four assists, in a 111–103 win over the [[Utah Jazz]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=DONCIC'S 31 POINTS PACE MAVS OVER NBA-LEADING JAZZ 111–103 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0022000764 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> For the second straight year, the Mavericks faced the Clippers during the first round of the playoffs. On May 22, Finney-Smith recorded 18 points and five rebounds in a 113–103 Game 1 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DONCIC HAS 31 POINTS, MAVS BEAT CLIPPERS 113–102 IN GAME 1 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000171 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> The Mavericks were eliminated by the Clippers in seven games, despite an 18-point, 10-rebound effort from Finney-Smith in the Mavericks' 126–111 Game 7 loss.<ref>{{Cite web |title=HOME SWEET HOME: CLIPPERS BEAT MAVS 126–111 TO WIN SERIES |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042000177 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref>

On February 12, 2022, Finney-Smith signed a four-year, $52 million veteran extension with the Mavericks.<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Dorian Finney-Smith Officially Signs New Mavs Contract; Mom Can Quit Working|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dorian-finney-smith-dallas-mavs-contract-extension-trade-deadline-official-mom#gid=ci029984590000278e&pid=dorian-finney-smith-on-the-challenge-call|access-date=February 23, 2022|magazine=Sports Illustrated | date=February 13, 2022 }}</ref> He scored a career-high 28 points on March 30 in a 120–112 win over the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]].<ref>{{Cite magazine|title=Dorian Finney-Smith's Career High Shows Growth For Mavs|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/dallas-mavs-dorian-finney-smith-career-high-western-conference-playoffs|access-date=March 30, 2022|magazine=Sports Illustrated}}</ref> The Mavericks beat the [[Utah Jazz]] in the first round of the playoffs and advanced to face the [[Phoenix Suns]] in the second round. On May 8, during the Mavericks' second-round series against the Suns, Finney-Smith scored a playoff career-high 24 points, alongside eight three-pointers and eight rebounds, in a 111–101 Game 4 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DONCIC, MAVS BEAT FOUL-PLAGUED PAUL, SUNS TO EVEN SERIES 2–2 |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100224 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref> The Mavericks defeated the Suns in seven games, but were eliminated in a five-game series in the [[NBA Conference Finals|Western Conference Finals]] by the [[Golden State Warriors]], who went on to win the [[NBA Finals]]. In Game 4 of the Conference Finals, Finney-Smith recorded 23 points, six rebounds and two assists in a 119–109 Game 4 win.<ref>{{Cite web |title=DONCIC, MAVS AVOID SWEEP WITH 119–109 WIN OVER WARRIORS |url=https://www.nba.com/game/0042100314 |access-date=February 6, 2023 |publisher=National Basketball Association}}</ref>

===Brooklyn Nets (2023–2024)===
On February 6, 2023, Finney-Smith was traded, alongside [[Spencer Dinwiddie]], an unprotected 2029 first-round pick, and second-round picks in 2027 and 2029, to the [[Brooklyn Nets]] in exchange for [[Kyrie Irving]] and [[Markieff Morris]].<ref>{{cite web |last1=Sefko |first1=Eddie |title=Kyrie Irving coming to the Mavericks |url=https://www.mavs.com/kyrie-trade/ |website=Dallas Mavericks |date=February 6, 2023 |access-date=February 6, 2023}}</ref>

=== Los Angeles Lakers (2024–2025) ===
On December 29, 2024, Finney-Smith was traded from the Nets alongside [[Shake Milton]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] in exchange for [[Maxwell Lewis]], [[D'Angelo Russell]] and three future second-round picks.<ref>{{cite web|title=Los Angeles Lakers Acquire Dorian Finney-Smith and Shake Milton|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/news/los-angeles-lakers-acquire-dorian-finney-smith-and-shake-milton-122924|website=NBA.com|date=December 29, 2024|access-date=December 29, 2024}}</ref> He became a valuable [[3-and-D]] player for the Lakers, helping them secure a No. 3 seed in the playoffs. He made 43 appearances (20 starts) for Los Angeles during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 7.9 points, 3.6 rebounds, and 1.4 assists. On June 12, 2025, Finney-Smith underwent surgery to repair a lingering ankle injury.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Sources: Lakers' Dorian Finney-Smith undergoes ankle surgery|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/45500661/sources-lakers-dorian-finney-smith-undergoes-ankle-surgery|access-date=September 28, 2025|website=espn.com|language=en}}</ref> On June 29, it was announced that Finney-Smith would be opting out of his $15.4 million player option Lakers contract for the 25-26 season to become an unrestricted free agent.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Dorian Finney-Smith Reportedly Opts Out of $15.4M Lakers Contract to Test Free Agency |website=[[Bleacher Report]] |url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/25175612-dorian-finney-smith-reportedly-opts-out-154m-lakers-contract-test-free-agency}}</ref>

=== Houston Rockets (2025–2026) ===
On July 7, 2025, Finney-Smith signed a four-year, $53 million contract with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Dorian Finney-Smith |url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-dorian-finney-smith |access-date=July 8, 2025 |website=Houston Rockets}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | last=Adams | first=Luke | title=Dorian Finney-Smith Signs Four-Year Contract With Rockets | website=Hoops Rumors | date=2025-06-30 | url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2025/06/dorian-finney-smith-to-sign-four-year-contract-with-rockets.html | access-date=2025-12-10}}</ref> Finney-Smith made 37 total appearances (including one start) for Houston during the [[2025–26 NBA season]], recording averages of 3.3 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 1.0 assist.

=== Charlotte Hornets (2026–present) ===
On July 6, 2026, Finney-Smith was traded to the [[Charlotte Hornets]] alongside three second round picks (2027, 2028 and 2033) in exchange for cash considerations.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Charlotte Hornets Acquire Finney-Smith And Three Second-Round Picks|url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/news/charlotte-hornets-acquire-finney-smith-and-three-second-round-picks |access-date=2026-07-07 |date=2026-07-06 |website=NBA.com}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Finney-Smith was born to Elbert Smith and Desiree Finney-Henderson.<ref name=wright/> He was nicknamed "Doe-Doe" after his paternal grandmother, Doris.<ref name=wright/> In 1996, Elbert was sentenced to 44 years in prison for his role in the 1995 murder of a man in [[Kempsville, Virginia]]; he was released from prison in 2024.<ref name=wright/> Finney-Smith's mother has five other children including three collegiate athletes: Ben Finney who played for the [[Old Dominion Monarchs men's basketball|Old Dominion Monarchs]], Sha-Kilya Finney who played for [[Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks women's basketball|Maryland Eastern Shore Hawks]], and Monnazjea Finney-Smith who played for the [[VCU Rams women's basketball|VCU Rams]].<ref name=harry>{{cite web |last1=Harry |first1=Chris |title=Tragedy to Triumph: 'Doe-Doe' Matures into UF Stalwart |url=https://floridagators.com/news/2014/11/14/29182 |website=University of Florida |access-date=July 15, 2025 |date=November 14, 2014}}</ref>

On September 13, 2008, Finney-Smith watched his older brother, Ra-Shawn Finney, as he was fatally shot seven times after a confrontation at a house party in [[Chesapeake, Virginia]].<ref name=harry/> Finney-Smith has Ra-Shawn's name tattooed across his chest.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Thomsen |first1=Ian |title=Rookie Dorian Finney-Smith quietly makes way for himself in Dallas |url=https://www.nba.com/news/mavericks-rookie-dorian-finney-smith-makes-way-himself |website=NBA |access-date=July 15, 2025 |date=December 18, 2016}}</ref>

Finney-Smith had his first child, a daughter, when he was 16 years old.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Jolee |first1=Tamara |title=Meet The Women Who Impacted Dorian Finney-Smith's life |url=https://www.mavs.com/doriansdestiny/ |website=Dallas Mavericks |access-date=July 15, 2025 |date=March 4, 2020}}</ref> He also has two sons.<ref name=wright>{{cite web |last1=Wright |first1=Michael C. |title='I can't thank them enough:' How the Mavs helped Dorian Finney-Smith reunite with his father |url=https://www.nba.com/news/dorian-finney-smith-elbert-smith-fathers-day |website=NBA |access-date=July 15, 2025 |date=June 16, 2024}}</ref>
